gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CKL's two HDMI 2.1 '8K60 / 4K144' dual-monitor KVMs, which share the same headline specs, differ on EDID emulation: the 922HUA-4 ($169) has none and the 922HUA-5 ($189) has it. None of them states either that '4K 60 Hz' on an HDMI 2.0-class KVM such as the UGREEN CM664 or the CKL 922HUA-3 gives full 4:4:4 colour only at 8-bit, so 10-bit HDR at 4K60 has to drop chroma resolution.
standout_why: I compared five rival pages. dockgearhq.com (HDMI picks) gives 4:4:4 8-bit and 18 Gbps only for the gofanco KVMHD2-2P, and only says UGREEN 'does not establish' EDID emulation. thetechsearch.com says UGREEN doesn't advertise EDID and that TESmart dual-monitor has it. deskdna.com and officekithq.com give no chroma, bandwidth or EDID detail for HDMI models. thisusb.com wouldn't load because of a certificate error. None covers CKL at all. None says that the same headline spec ('HDMI 2.1, 8K60, 4K144') hides a model with no EDID emulation. None explains what '4K60' means for HDR colour on HDMI 2.0-class switches.
decides: It sorts the dual-monitor pick ChatGPT showed (CKL, $139.99 to $359 TESmart). If you need high refresh and don't want windows rearranging on every switch, the CKL 922HUA-5 ($189) is the pick, not the 922HUA-4 ($169), even though both list the same resolutions. The TESmart HKS202-M24 at $359 lists EDID emulation and hotkeys but gives no chroma or DSC detail for its 4K144 mode. For a one-monitor 4K60 office setup, the UGREEN CM664 still holds: its manual lists RGB/4:4:4 output. But it has no hotkey switching, and the manual is silent on EDID. Buyers who want 4K60 HDR on any HDMI 2.0 KVM should expect subsampled chroma.
